title: Unified telemetry normalizer with tenant-aware sampling and correlation signpost
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem: Our current ingest fabric accepts heterogeneous log payloads and performs only lightweight enrichment. We lack a single canonical normalization step that: (1) enforces a minimal structured-log schema, (2) attaches deterministic correlation signposts for cross-surface joins, and (3) applies tenant-aware adaptive sampling to control downstream cost without losing high-fidelity signal for errors and SLO breaches. Without this, debugging multi-hop traces across runtime, routing, and console is slow and costly.

Goals: Implement a Unified Telemetry Normalizer (UTN) that: 
- Accepts multi-format input (JSON, key=value, protobuf) and outputs canonical structured logs (RFC-style fields: timestamp, service, span_id, trace_id, correlation_signpost, level, msg, attrs).
- Generates a deterministic "correlation_signpost" derived from trace_id/span_id/tenant_id to create cheap join keys for quick dashboards and sampling.
- Performs tenant-aware adaptive sampling: default deterministic sample by hashed correlation_signpost with override rules when error-rate or SLO anomaly is detected.
- Supports dynamic routing to Loki (for raw streams) and Elasticsearch (for enriched indexed search) with configurable sampling knobs per tenant via feature flags or a schema-backed config store.
- Applies PII/redaction rules (GDPR) before export and records redaction metadata in the normalized payload.
- Maintains ingest latency < 100ms p95 and < 2s p99 under standard load; does not increase downstream error rate.

Design notes and trade-offs: 
- Deterministic sampling: use FNV-1a 64-bit hash over correlation_signpost + tenant_id to allow consistent patient rehydration when full traces are requested. Avoid random sampling to preserve stable trace membership. 
- Signpost generation: prefer existing trace_id when present; otherwise synthesize stable signpost using request_id or a hashed combination of client_ip + user_agent + timestamp-bucket. Documented in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/UTN-design.
- Schema registry: add a lightweight versioned schema with validation hooks in the normalizer (reject/route-to-dead-letter for invalid messages). Use schema versions as top-level attribute to allow downstream consumers to opt-in.
- Tenant-aware rules: default sample_rate = tenant_profile.sample_rate; if tenant_profile.is_platinum then sample_rate=1.0; if error_rate > threshold then sample_rate = max(sample_rate, error_boost). These rules live in a config store (featureflags.redwood.ai) and are hot-reloadable.
- Backpressure and resource throttling: when normalizer queue > 80% capacity, reduce sampling for non-error logs and emit a monitor metric ingest.queue_overflow. Guarantee dropped-data metric is exported to the console so we can alert.

Acceptance criteria: 
- End-to-end pipeline demo: generate mixed-format traffic and show canonical logs in ES and raw+sampled streams in Loki.
- p95 ingest-to-export latency < 100ms and p99 < 2s for 95th percentile traffic tested in staging.
- Deterministic sampling reproduces same membership when replaying identical events.
- Redaction policy applied for configured PII fields and redaction_count visible per-event.
- Can enable/disable the feature via feature-flag per-tenant and roll back without schema breaking.

Rollout plan: 
1) Deploy normalizer to staging behind a feature-flag with tenant=internal-only. Run A/B traffic for 72 hours. Dashboards: telemetry.ingest.latency.p95, telemetry.ingest.p99, telemetry.import.error-rate, telemetry.sampling.effective_rate.
2) Canary to 5 pilot tenants (low volume) and monitor for 48 hours.
3) Incrementally enable tenant profiles with 10x, 50x traffic ramps. If dropped_event_rate > 0.1% or p99 latency doubles, rollback.

Testing strategy: 
- Unit tests for schema validation and deterministic hash.
- Integration tests that replay recorded traces and assert membership stability.
- Load tests in perf cluster with synthetic tenant mix; baseline against current ingest path.
- Manual privacy review where PII redaction rules are validated by Privacy team.

Operational runbooks and dashboards: 
- Create runbook entry: "UTN: dropped events and sampling anomalies" with step-by-step triage.
- Dashboards: per-tenant sampling rate, dropped_events, queue_length, p95/p99 latency, exports to Loki/ES success rate.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: misconfigured sampling could under-sample errors. Mitigation: default error-boost rule (always sample 100% of error and WARN level logs for first N minutes after anomaly detection).
- Risk: added CPU for normalization increases cost. Mitigation: offload heavy ops (PII regex) to workers and allow opt-in via tenant profile.
- Risk: schema changes break consumers. Mitigation: version field and consumer compatibility checks in release notes.

Artifacts: 
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/UTN-design (internal)
- Perf benchmark PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/612 (WIP)
- Initial implementation branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/tree/feature/utn-normalizer (WIP)
